image_description: A close-up view of a large whale's head emerging vertically from deep blue water. The rostrum is arched and covered in mottled grey skin with distinct white patches (barnacles/cyamids). The mouth appears slightly open or the angle highlights the ventral pleats/texture. No dorsal fin is visible in this specific crop, focusing entirely on the head and anterior body.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is relatively short with arched rostrum and two blowholes on top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly displays the characteristic arched rostrum of a grey whale. While the blowholes are at the very peak and partially obscured by the angle/lighting, the overall head shape and arch are diagnostic and present.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The skin texture is highly detailed, showing the specific mottled grey coloration and numerous white callosities/barnacle patches typical of Eschrichtius gibbosus.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image is cropped tightly on the head and shoulders; the posterior back where dorsal knuckles would be located is outside the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Robust spindle-shaped body of enormous proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Only the anterior portion of the body is visible; the full spindle shape cannot be verified due to cropping.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey with white patches created by barnacles.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Consistent with the head checkpoint, the visible upper body skin exhibits the correct mottling and barnacle distribution.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Baleen plates are cream-colored, densely packed in numerous rows along each side.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth is not sufficiently open or angled to reveal the internal baleen plates; they are occluded.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flippers (pectoral fins) are broad and paddle-shaped, remarkably elongated relative to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The pectoral fins are submerged or outside the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail flukes are broad with smooth trailing edge and central notch.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is completely outside the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin texture is rough with callosities.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The high-resolution texture on the head confirms the rough, callosity-covered skin structure.

alignment_reasoning: All testable checkpoints for the visible portion of the animal (head shape, skin mottling, barnacle distribution, texture) are perfectly met. The image is a textbook example of a grey whale head. Non-testable checkpoints are due to framing, not absence or error.
artifact_reasoning: No AI artifacts detected. Water interaction, lighting reflections, and biological textures appear physically consistent and photorealistic. Edges are sharp without bleeding or melting.
